comparator.name: Sociology (Sociologie)
comparator.sourceNotes: Tilburg’s current official 2026–27 curriculum accounts for exactly 180 ECTS. Year 1 is a fixed 60-ECTS sociology foundation. Year 2 combines 36 ECTS of common methods, philosophy and research with the 24-ECTS Grootstedelijke Vraagstukken major. The selected non-exchange Year 3 route contains a 12-ECTS placement, an 18-ECTS minor, 12 ECTS of compulsory Sociology electives, a 12-ECTS thesis and 6 ECTS of Social Philosophy. This is the published route used to complete the curriculum without inventing exchange or elective content.
components: Required in the published non-exchange route used to complete the 180-ECTS curriculum.
Structured minor space; no particular minor is invented.
Compulsory Sociology elective space; no unpublished option list is invented.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is Tilburg’s Dutch Sociology bachelor, which focuses on Dutch society. Of the three published majors, Grootstedelijke Vraagstukken is the Dutch-taught route and directly continues the programme’s stated attention to Dutch cities, inequality, exclusion and the welfare state. It is selected independently of UCR fit.

core: Sociological theories of social interaction, institutions, cohesion and social change
Social inequality, poverty, exclusion, welfare and urban life
Qualitative, quantitative and mixed sociological research using surveys, statistics and projects
Relationships among individuals, groups, institutions, society and public policy
Academic sociological craft and independent research culminating in a thesis
adjacent: Public policy, institutions and collective responses to social problems
Migration, culture, family and identities in comparative perspective
Climate, health, work and sustainability as social risks in changing societies
questions: What structures and mechanisms produce inequality and changing social problems?
How do institutions, culture and collective action reproduce or change social relations?
How can qualitative and quantitative evidence explain social patterns and change?

alternatives.label: Sociology, urban inequality & public policy
alternatives.concept: Builds a broad sociological programme around theory, institutions, inequality, urban social problems and public policy, supported by qualitative inquiry, statistics, data analysis and an applied research sequence.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum contains the full available UCR sociology sequence plus inequality, institutions, public policy and a substantial qualitative and quantitative research spine.
progression: Introductory sociology, institutions, research and statistics precede modern theory, inequality, qualitative and quantitative analysis, public health, global relations and advanced social research. All prerequisites and planned offerings pass; seven 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Culture, identity & migration in comparative perspective
alternatives.concept: Studies migration, cultural difference, family, identity and inequality through comparative sociology, histories of empire and gender, global political economy and transnational politics.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed programme shifts the centre of gravity to migration, culture, identity, empire and transnational comparison while retaining a coherent sociology and research sequence.
alternatives.distinctness: This route replaces most domestic-policy, quantitative and public-health content with histories of empire and gender, international relations and law, global political economy, race, Indigenous histories and political psychology. It differs by at least eight courses from the closest programme.
progression: Sociology, politics, history and research foundations precede global political economy, migration-related inequality, race, citizenship, identity, international law and advanced transnational analysis. All prerequisites and planned offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Social risks, health & sustainability
alternatives.concept: Examines how climate change, public health, work, welfare and governance create and distribute social risks, combining sociology with sustainability science, public economics, psychology and policy analysis.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed programme visibly integrates sociology with climate, health, sustainability governance, welfare economics and public communication around changing social risks.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest programme, this route replaces gender history, global law, advanced econometrics and public persuasion with sustainability foundations, climate science, sustainability governance, public economics and climate communication. It differs by at least five courses from each earlier programme.
progression: Sociology, sustainability, health, research and statistics foundations precede climate communication, public economics, governance, political psychology and advanced applied research. All prerequisites and planned offerings pass; seven 300-level courses are included.

selection.assessment: The closest programme uses the complete available UCR sociology sequence and a strong mixed-method social-research spine. The culture/identity/migration and social-risks/health/sustainability directions are independently supported by generator-eligible programme interests and the official curriculum, produce substantively different course choices, and pass feasibility and pairwise distinctness. Production therefore stops at the three-alternative maximum.

notes.text: Tilburg Sociology provides a continuous disciplinary sequence in theory, qualitative and quantitative methods, survey construction, causal analysis, major-specific courses, sociological research projects and a 12-ECTS thesis. UCR offers a coherent sociology core and strong related study in politics, history, psychology, economics, media and research methods, but it does not reproduce the same continuous specialist sociology sequence.

UCR does not reproduce Tilburg’s dedicated survey-construction course, full causal-analysis sequence, 12-ECTS second-year sociological research project, complete Metropolitan Social Issues major, placement structure or 12-ECTS sociology thesis. Those differences remain explicit rather than being filled with weak substitutes.
The selected Tilburg Sociology route is Dutch-taught, while UCR is English-taught. The comparison assesses academic content and structure rather than language eligibility.
